passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: On the 14th anniversary of the Short family murders, the Henry County Sheriff’s Office renewed its public appeal for information concerning the unsolved killings of Michael, Mary and Jennifer Short.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Sheriff’s Office released a case flyer identifying all three members of the Short family as murder victims and summarized the investigation:

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael and Mary Short were found murdered inside their Bassett, Virginia, home on August 15, 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Both had suffered a single gunshot wound to the head.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Their 9-year-old daughter, Jennifer Renee Short, was missing from the residence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s body was discovered on September 25, 2002, underneath a bridge in Stoneville, Rockingham County, North Carolina.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer had also suffered a single gunshot wound to the head.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The murders remained unsolved.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff Lane Perry and Rockingham County Sheriff Sam Page urged anyone with information, no matter how insignificant it might seem, to contact investigators.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Short Family Home Destroyed: The former Short family residence burned to the ground.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities said they did not believe the fire was connected to the 2002 murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators also said they believed all usable evidence had already been removed from the residence during the original investigation and that destruction of the house would not materially damage the homicide investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: New Multi-Agency Task Force: Henry County Sheriff Lane Perry assembled a new multi-agency task force to conduct a comprehensive review of the Short family murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators were instructed to review the case in its entirety.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The task force specifically began examining physical evidence preserved from 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators wanted to determine whether advances in forensic science could produce information that had been impossible to obtain when the evidence was originally collected. This included the possibility of new DNA analysis.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The reward at that time was $62,500 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or persons responsible.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Task Force Finds New Leads: Officials reported that the renewed task-force review had generated several new leads. The investigation remained active as the 20th anniversary approached.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: 20th Anniversary: Twenty years had passed since Michael and Mary were murdered and Jennifer was abducted. No one had been charged.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Community members continued memorial events honoring the Short family and maintaining public awareness of the unsolved case.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Second Fresh-Eyes Task Force: Henry County Sheriff Wayne Davis authorized another focused task-force effort. Davis had been one of the patrol officers responding to the Short residence in 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Their purpose was to review decades of reports, interviews, tips, and physical evidence without relying solely on conclusions reached by earlier investigative teams.
